Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Policy

The manifesto centres on economic stability, citing reduced inflation (from 11.1% to 2.3%), returning growth, and rising real wages. Key tax proposals include:

- Halving employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027
- Abolishing the main rate of self-employed National Insurance
- Introducing a "Triple Lock Plus" for pensioners, guaranteeing the State Pension and pensioner tax-free allowance rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%
- Maintaining current rates of income tax, VAT, and Capital Gains Tax
- Reforming Child Benefit to a household basis, with thresholds set at £120,000-£160,000

The manifesto commits to meeting fiscal rules requiring falling public sector net debt and borrowing below 3% of GDP.

## Immigration

Proposals include:

- Introducing a legally binding annual cap on migration
- Continuing deportation flights to Rwanda for illegal migrants
- Working to reform international asylum treaties
- Raising visa salary thresholds and health requirements for migrants

## Public Services

**NHS**: Commitments include above-inflation funding increases annually, recruiting 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors, expanding Pharmacy First, building 250 GP surgeries, and 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.

**Education**: Plans include mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds (military or civic), 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing underperforming university courses, banning mobile phones in schools during the school day, and introducing the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education.

## Housing and Infrastructure

- Target of 1.6 million new homes in England
- Abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules to unlock 100,000 homes
- Permanent Stamp Duty abolition for first-time buyers on homes up to £425,000
- New Help to Buy scheme
- £36 billion transport investment from cancelled HS2 phase two, including £8.3 billion for roads

## Defence and Security

- Increasing defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030
- Continued support for Ukraine
- Investment in nuclear deterrent and new defence technologies
- £10 billion investment in UK munitions production

## Energy and Environment

- Annual licensing rounds for North Sea oil and gas
- Trebling offshore wind capacity
- Building new nuclear capacity including Small Modular Reactors
- Commitment to net zero by 2050 with a "pragmatic" approach
- No new green levies on household bills

## Welfare Reform

- Reforming disability benefits assessment
- Tightening work capability assessments
- Introducing sanctions removing benefits after 12 months for those refusing suitable work
- Projected savings of £12 billion annually

## Devolution and Union

The manifesto commits to maintaining the UK internal market, extending levelling up funding across Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, and opposing Scottish independence while implementing the Windsor Framework commitments for Northern Ireland.

# Liberal Democrats 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Economy and Business
The manifesto proposes investing in renewable energy and home insulation, creating apprenticeships and Lifelong Skills Grants, reforming business rates, and managing public finances responsibly. Plans include fixing UK-EU trade relations, replacing the apprenticeship levy with a broader skills levy, and expanding the British Business Bank. Tax proposals include reversing bank tax cuts, increasing Digital Services Tax to 6%, and reforming capital gains tax.

## Health and Care
The party commits to guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases) through recruiting 8,000 additional GPs. Proposals include NHS dental access guarantees, mental health hubs for young people, a 62-day cancer treatment target, and free personal care based on Scotland's model. A new Carer's Minimum Wage (£2/hour increase) and cross-party commission on social care funding are proposed.

## Education
Plans include placing mental health professionals in every school, increasing school funding above inflation, introducing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, and reinstating maintenance grants. Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education are proposed, alongside free school meal expansion for children in poverty.

## Housing
The manifesto targets 380,000 new homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through garden cities and brownfield development. Renters would receive protection through banned no-fault evictions and three-year default tenancies. Proposals include abolishing residential leasehold and ending rough sleeping within the Parliament.

## Environment
Environmental plans include a sewage tax on water company profits, legally binding targets to "double nature" by 2050, planting 60 million trees annually, and a Clean Air Act. The party aims for net zero by 2045 and 90% renewable electricity by 2030.

## Transport
Proposals include expanding EV charging infrastructure, reinstating plug-in car grants, freezing rail fares, extending rail electrification, and boosting bus services with local authority franchising powers. Road maintenance funding would shift to local councils for pothole repairs.

## Immigration and Asylum
The manifesto proposes scrapping the Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda scheme, processing asylum claims within three months, and allowing asylum seekers to work after three months. Work visa policy would transfer from the Home Office, and Youth Mobility Scheme expansion with the EU is proposed.

## Political Reform
Proposals include introducing proportional representation (Single Transferable Vote) for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, enshrining the Ministerial Code in law, reforming the House of Lords, capping political donations, and scrapping voter ID requirements.

## Defence and International
Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP, with Army cuts reversed. The party supports NATO, maintaining nuclear deterrence, and Ukraine. European relations would follow a four-stage roadmap toward closer cooperation, ultimately aiming for Single Market membership. International development spending would return to 0.7% of national income.
